SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Endoscopy Procedure Report (fictional)
Date of service: October 30, 2026
Endoscopist: Rowan Ellery, MD (fictional)
Patient: Test Patient Hollis (fictional) | MRN: SYN-48213
Procedures: Upper endoscopy and colonoscopy.
Indications: Progressive solid-food dysphagia; iron-deficiency anemia; surveillance after a prior polypectomy in
2023.
Sedation: Monitored anesthesia care was provided by the anesthesia service.
Upper endoscopy
The gastroscope was advanced through the mouth to the second portion of the duodenum. A short, smooth
peptic stricture
was found in the distal esophagus at 36 cm, narrowing the lumen to about 11 mm. A through-the-scope balloon
was passed
across the stricture and inflated to 13.5 mm and then 15 mm under direct vision; mild mucosal disruption followed
and
there was no deep tear. In the gastric body a 6 mm sessile polyp was removed with a cold snare and retrieved.
Random
biopsies of the second portion of the duodenum were taken with cold forceps to evaluate for celiac disease. The
stomach
was suctioned and the gastroscope was withdrawn.
Colonoscopy
The colonoscope was advanced to the cecum, identified by the appendiceal orifice and the ileocecal valve. The
bowel
preparation was adequate. In the transverse colon an 8 mm pedunculated polyp was removed with a hot snare
and
retrieved. In the sigmoid colon a separate 4 mm sessile polyp was removed with cold biopsy forceps. In the
ascending
colon a 25 mm laterally spreading lesion with a central depression was photographed and not removed; it is
referred
for endoscopic resection at a later session. Sterile carbon tattoo ink was injected into the submucosa just distal to
the ascending colon lesion to mark its site. Small internal hemorrhoids were seen on retroflexion.
Impression
Distal esophageal peptic stricture, dilated with a balloon to 15 mm. Gastric body polyp removed by cold snare.
Duodenal biopsies taken. Transverse colon polyp removed by hot snare. Sigmoid polyp removed by cold forceps.
Ascending
colon laterally spreading lesion marked with tattoo and left in place for planned resection.
Plan
Advance the diet as tolerated. Await pathology. Schedule endoscopic mucosal resection of the ascending colon
lesion.
Electronically signed by Rowan Ellery, MD (fictional), October 30, 2026
